reasoning: Both sets are rigorous, well-structured multi-package plans with strong quant discipline: point-in-time reads, delisting returns, per-window PCA, Marchenko–Pastur denoising, routing of the hypothesis-testing skill, and an M1 walking skeleton on synthetic data with good golden cases. A wins narrowly because it covers the brief more completely. It plans all four stages, including the PPO trading agents, rented-GPU training with verified teardown, a hypothesis ledger, a lockbox, and a final verdict judged against the stored classical portfolios. It also has a clean single Phase 0 interface and a sound dependency graph. A's main failings are real, though. It drops the user's yahooquery cross-check entirely and never uses the user's 10-name delisted list. It adds an EDGAR sector source the user never asked for. It has no CONSTRAINTS.md even though every packet tells the builder to read it. B keeps the Yahoo cross-check and the 10-name reference list. Its M1 is a richer slice: runs started from the app with live WebSocket progress, reload survival, search and company pages. But B leaves out the PPO agents ('a separate, later idea' with no stage or milestone) and rules out cloud compute ('Cloud compute; every model trains on the user's machine'), which contradicts the user's occasional rented GPU. B's brief is still framed around stage 1 only. It runs three interface tasks in parallel even though they import each other's types, and it labels many tasks 'spine' while giving them Kind thicken and Mode split. Both sets wrongly use Nasdaq Data Link instead of the user's api.sharadar.com. On balance, B's gap removes a whole S4 component and the planned compute model, while A's gap is one validation source plus a missing quality-bar file.
